0.comment: The Tsaritsa: Saarelainen and the erased past
0.content:
Anastasya's lover more than 6,000 years ago was Saarelainen, the Third Descender, who came from the sea of stars. They had a son with four-pointed star pupils, the ancestor of the Khaenri'ahns. When the Heavenly Principles erased her for opening the Abyss gate, Saarelainen offered his body, to be split into the seven Gnoses, for her revival and for their descendants' safety, sealing the promise with a curse that would put the Heavenly Principles to sleep if broken. Every trace of him was then erased, including from her mind.

The Belyi Tsar, who had fled into the Shadow Realm, kept the memory and told her; she did not trust the story, and it never felt real. In 7.1 Rhinedottir retold it over tea. She called Saarelainen naive for bargaining with a higher being, deduced that the Cataclysm triggered his curse and put the Heavenly Principles to sleep, and said only that she chooses to live in the present. She added that she has never known how to face the Khaenri'ahns, her descendants.

Rhinedottir offered her a title of respect, 'Mother of Khaenri'ah', and said Khaenri'ah would have been proud of such a mother; the Tsaritsa fell silent. The Hymns of the Far North, whose reliability is disputed, say Saarelainen crossed Hiisi Island and Pohjola to court her at her home.

1.content:
Her predecessor, Monomakh Snezhnyi, was the first Cryo Archon and God of Love, an incomplete Primordial Human who believed himself fae. He incited Anastasya and Saarelainen to open the Abyss gate, then hid in the Shadow Realm; guilty, he later told her what had been erased, but she never trusted him. He died fighting the Abyss in the Cataclysm. She took his throne, palace and a feminine form of his surname, but dismantled his fae aristocracy.

He founded Kitezh, the first city of Snezhnaya, and unified the fae. Since his death the Snowland Fae nobility has lost most of its former influence. He watched over the Third Descender's seal until his death; she took over that duty.

2.content:
Because Celestia altered memories and history through Irminsul, Anastasya distrusts recollection. Each day she records the day's events in a Transcription Prism, a device carrying the Third Descender's power and therefore outside certain laws of Teyvat; Irminsul changes cannot alter it. She pauses audiences to 'complete today's memory recording', and Pierro explained the habit to the Traveler.

The Armory Palace's Mirror of Remembrance (Svetovid Stone) is a related, larger prism that can store memories and draw them from nearby people. The wiki suggests the prism is why she knows of Scaramouche despite his self-erasure; this is inference.

3.comment: The Tsaritsa: The Gnoses and the seal beneath the palace
3.content:
She holds six Gnoses: her own Cryo and the Anemo, Geo, Electro, Dendro and Hydro Gnoses. Signora took the Anemo from Venti and received the Geo from Zhongli; Dottore claimed Electro and Dendro; Arlecchino received the Hydro from Neuvillette as a diplomatic gift. Only the Pyro Gnosis is missing, and it burned with Irminsul and returned to the Ley Lines. She expects the Ley Lines to excise it eventually.

The Gnoses are remains of the Third Descender and do not originate within Teyvat's system. Fully exploited they allow power beyond an Archon's authority. Beneath Zapolyarny Palace lies a seal he left; the Belyi Tsar guarded it before her, it reacts only to Gnoses, and every attempt to open it has failed. She believes opening it needs all seven. Before Signora's funeral she played chess against Pierro using the Anemo and Geo Gnoses as pieces.

4.comment: The Tsaritsa: Rhinedottir's tea and Ronova's fall
4.content:
In 7.1 the Tsaritsa let it be known that she was collecting Seals of Life, drawing the Ruler of Life out into the open. At the Northland Bank the two met; she offered intelligence on Asmoday for a meeting in seven days. At the meeting she asked directly how the Heavenly Principles were and when they would wake; Rhinedottir refused but stayed for tea after the Tsaritsa called Snezhnaya Celestia's rival.

While they talked, she used six Gnoses and her Cryo mastery to slow time in the hall, so that Rhinedottir missed the window to revive Ronova's victims before Celestia's next monitoring cycle. Celestia revoked Ronova's authority; the Curse of Death lapsed and Rhinedottir had to revive the dead. 'I don't believe in sacrificing pawns', she said. Naberius wanted punishment; Rhinedottir declined, called her a worthy rival, and said Snezhnaya might achieve monumental things.

5.content:
Pierro, the Khaenri'ahn Eftirvit, reached Snezhnaya after the Cataclysm and shared her hatred of the world's foundational principles. In the third year of her reign she founded the Fatui under his leadership. He relays her appointments, outlines her plans to the Harbingers, and declared in her name at Nasha Town that even the gods have their limits.

She trusts him with Project Mistilteinn and with Ronova; she accepted his advice to seal Hroptatyr's forbidden notebook. He tells the Traveler that some of her plans are not his to disclose. After the Eye of the Fatui drained him in 7.1, she commended everyone who took part.

6.content:
Vesna and Danica are the Tsaritsa's closest attendants. Vesna, Commander of the Druzhna and a Vila, handles military decrees. Danica, her Head Maid and trusted personal attendant, comes from a family that has served the Tsaritsa for three generations. Both were trained by the same mentor, identified in official material as Capitano.

Vesna says the Tsaritsa adds 'rest well' to decrees and that she returned the unclaimed portion of the Ruler of Life's power after it was reclaimed. Danica says the Tsaritsa let her follow her own wishes and persuaded her mother and grandmother to let her travel. When Danica questioned the Traveler harshly at Podvorye Restaurant, the Tsaritsa told her her methods risked a friend's trust.

7.comment: The Tsaritsa: The Traveler as Consultant
7.content:
After 7.0 the Tsaritsa received the Traveler at court, called them a formidable adversary worthy of respect, ended all investigations into them and granted unrestricted palace access. Later, after Vesna and Danica disagreed over whether the Traveler needed more time, she explained that she needed outside eyes to understand a nation she was 'supposed to... love': ministers are biased by their relationship to her, and she cannot walk the streets (Danica would never allow it).

Since the Traveler would not swear fealty, she made them 'Consultant to the Tsaritsa', a special envoy with authority and resources, with requests routed through Chayka. She accepted their promise to travel her nation as they travelled others: by telling stories and noticing small things.

8.comment: The Tsaritsa: Portraits of the Tsaritsa
8.content:
At a minister's suggestion, she asked the Traveler to learn how the public sees her. Alyosha, Odette and Vodyanitsa commissioned a Fontaine artist's 'The Tsaritsa in Spring', meant to warm a home. Pulcinella, Pantalone, Sandrone and Arlecchino together proposed a cold, stern portrait to deter hostile factions. Chayka painted her as a Domovoy.

She accepted all three: the Harbingers' hangs in Glupov, 'The Tsaritsa in Spring' in the Korolevskiy theatre, and Chayka's in the streets of Zapolyarny. She said that although Snezhnaya has but one Tsaritsa, each person sees her differently, and that they should be free to depict her as they wish.

9.comment: The Tsaritsa: Rise to power and the fae princes
9.content:
After being crowned in the first year of the 799th Cycle, the Tsaritsa faced fae princes who would not seek an audience and a human uprising at Port Belovodye. She formed the Fatui, took the Drevogorye, Volkhovan and Cirnareka lands for negligence and condoning rebellion, forced absent princes to trade authority for titles, and offered Belovodye amnesty or destruction. The rebellion ended without more fighting.

Glupov, the Snezhnograd Veche (under the human Ioanna Ivanovna) and the Imperial Order Reformation Edict followed; many fae renounced titles and left. These details come from the in-game history book A Brief History of the Pale Starborn.

10.content:
She is the God of Love, as the Belyi Tsar was. She does not identify with the authority and does not intend to use it. In her view the Heavenly Principles carved love for humanity into the gods' bones, so it is not true love. Pierro says all the world's rules are curses; a god's love for humanity is one of them.

She says she chooses her true self and her duties as Tsaritsa. Vesna disagrees with her definition, citing her small mercies; Columbina and Tartaglia describe a hidden or too-gentle heart. Dainsleif dislikes court occasions but says she is different, and he could not deny the Mother of Khaenri'ah a straightforward audience.

11.comment: The Tsaritsa: Venti and the broken ties
11.content:
Venti says he knew the Tsaritsa well, but after the Cataclysm five hundred years ago she cut off all ties. He has not seen her since and wonders what she is thinking and planning. Her Harbingers took his Anemo Gnosis, and canon gives no reason for the break.

In 7.1 the Traveler remembered Venti's words that freedom demanded by an archon is no freedom at all, in connection with her stance on the authority of love. Venti was not present.

12.comment: The Tsaritsa: Capitano, Mavuika and the Pyro Gnosis
12.content:
Capitano dueled Mavuika for her Gnosis but declined to exploit her weakness and asked the Tsaritsa to be relieved of the task; she agreed. When he later died taking revenge on Ronova, she let his rank stand. Mavuika suspected she would send another Harbinger for the Pyro Gnosis.

In 7.1 the Traveler told her the Pyro Gnosis burned with Irminsul and returned to the Ley Lines. She noted it could not coexist with the Ley Lines for long and would be excised, and said she would find it in time.

13.comment: The Tsaritsa: Arlecchino, Columbina and the Harbingers
13.content:
The Harbingers all answer to her and are appointed by her, directly or through Pierro. She named Columbina and made her Third Harbinger around three or four centuries ago. A little over ten years ago she pardoned the House of the Hearth orphan Peruere for killing a Harbinger and made her the Knave, Arlecchino. Tartaglia, Arlecchino and Columbina each voice differing views of her.

Columbina fulfilled a promise to the Tsaritsa before leaving the Fatui; the Tsaritsa then issued the Palestar Edict ordering her capture and put three Harbingers in charge of Nod-Krai. After Dottore was found to have gone against her will, she let Arlecchino and Sandrone eliminate him if necessary and rescinded the edict.

14.comment: The Tsaritsa: Signora's funeral and the Geo contract
14.content:
Signora took the Geo Gnosis from Zhongli under a 'contract to end all contracts' that the Tsaritsa had offered him; he refused to explain it to Paimon. After Signora died in Inazuma, the Tsaritsa held her funeral at the Sanctuary of Grief, played chess against Pierro using the collected Gnoses, and froze the whole mausoleum.

All the Harbingers attended except Scaramouche, who had gone missing. Her presence was implied rather than shown: a cold moved the pieces and ice crept through the building.

15.comment: The Tsaritsa: Her goal against the Heavenly Principles
15.content:
She aims to challenge or overthrow the Heavenly Principles because Snezhnaya, forced to push technology to its limit, has long lived under threat of a Nail of Retribution. She told the Traveler 'civilization is but a lie told to us by fate' and that she is fighting to survive. Project Mistilteinn, an anti-Celestia weapon built with Stellar Linchpins, serves this goal.

She says the power of The Seven cannot shake the foundations of the world, which needs supreme authority. The Gnoses are the route to power beyond her limits, and the seal may hold something the Third Descender thought vital. After Ronova's authority was revoked, the Curse of Death on research lifted and Mistilteinn can move forward.
